A work permit UAE is necessary for foreigners who wish to work in the country. In addition, you must meet the requirements regarding qualifications and certifications appropriate for the position applied for. Likewise, the employer must comply with all the requirements demanded by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization.

In this article, let us show you details about work permit in UAE, such as the cost and application procedure. In the same way, you will learn about the mission work permit for specific and short-term tasks.

What is a work permit in UAE and how does it work?

A work permit UAE is a document that allows the holder to live and work in the country under the sponsorship of an employer. In this case, the worker can carry out their work for between 2 and 3 years with the possibility of renewing the permit. However, it is the decision of the employer whether to renew or cancel the work permit of the employee.

Although there are various work visa options, the standard one is the most commonly used by foreigners. To obtain the permit, the worker must have a signed contract and approval from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization (MoHRE). Furthermore, before being able to enter the country, the foreigner needs to obtain a job offer and an entry permit.

This is because you first need authorization to enter the UAE to begin the procedures. Thus, once in the country, the employer must begin with the application for a work and residence visa.

What is the processing time for obtaining a work permit in the UAE?

The entire permit process is easy to do and requires little time for approval or denial. However, you should consider that you need all the documentation required by MOHRE to consider the application. After that, the work permits in the UAE processing time is a maximum of 5 business days.

Step-by-step guide: how to obtain a work permit in the UAE?

Applying for a work permit involves well-defined stages and a very simple process. Next, we will show you how to get work permits in the UAE in just a few steps:

Work permit UAE Fee approval application

To begin, the hiring company must apply to MOHRE for approval of the work visa fee. The permit fees an employer can obtain depend on the office space of the company. For example, if an employer does business in Dubai, the fee is one permit per 9m² of office space.

This also applies to companies in Free Zones, which have a restriction depending on where they are located. Thus, if the employer has already reached the quota, they must move to a larger office or request a quota improvement.

Presentation of a signed employment contract

The next step to obtain a work permit UAE, after the quota approval, is to present the contract signed by both parties. In this case, the government body that approves or does not approve the contract, which must follow local regulations, is the MOHRE. Additionally, the contract must be in Arabic, English, and the language of the employee if it is not one of the above.

Work permit UAE application

The company that wishes to hire the foreigner must submit the work permit application to the MOHRE. In this way, the entity confirms the entity of the company and whether a national can occupy the position requested by the foreigner. After this approval, the employer may request an entry visa for the worker to legally enter the country.

The worker receives the entry visa

After approval of the work permits in the UAE, MOHRE will issue an entry visa to the worker. In this case, the visa is valid for 60 days and the employee may stay for 30 days, extendable to complete the procedures. In this way, the worker must carry out the application process for a residence visa, following a standard procedure.

For its part, the employer must carry out other procedures to formalize the work permit for the employee. For the worker to apply for a residence visa, he or she must apply for an Emirates ID and pass a medical checkup.

Applying for a UAE ID

Foreigners intending to work in the UAE must obtain an Emirates ID to continue the procedures. This is an essential requirement to request a medical examination that is within the work permits in the UAE requirements. This identification will be linked to your residence visa and you must have it with you at all times.

To apply for identification, go to an Emirates Identity Authority (EIDA) center, bringing your passport. You must also bring your entry visa, and a photograph, and register your biometric data (fingerprints).

Undergo a medical checkup

Without distinction, all work visa applicants must undergo a medical examination at an authorized clinic. You must pass this exam to continue with the work permit application process.

Presentation of the employment contract

The formalization of the work permits in the UAE requires the employer to upload the employment contract to the MOHRE website. Additionally, they must do so within 14 days of the results of the medical examination.

Get health insurance

All foreigners working in the UAE must take out health insurance that covers their entire stay. However, in certain Emirates, such as Abu Dhabi and Dubai, companies must provide this insurance to their employees and their families. This requirement is essential both for the issuance of a work visa and for its renewal.

Obtaining a work visa

After completing the entire previous process, you will have to wait about 5 business days to receive the work visa. In this way, the worker will be able to start working at the company and will only need to receive a residence visa.

Receive a residence visa

The employee must collect all the necessary documents to apply for the residence visa and receive the Emirates ID. The residence visa is valid for 2 years but you can renew it for the same period. In addition, the residence visa allows the foreigner to carry out various procedures in the country, including:

  • Open a bank account
  • Register a vehicle
  • Get a PO Box

What are the fees associated with getting a work permit in the UAE?

To obtain the document, the applicant must pay the work permits in  UAE fees, which are as follows:

  • The initial application for an electronic work permit regardless of category or level is AED 200.
  • The approval of the work permit depends on the categories as follows:
    • Category 1 costs AED 300
    • Category 2, depending on the level, has a cost of AED 600 Level A, AED 1500 Level B, and AED 2000 Level C
    • The category 3 costs AED 5000

In the same way, the work permit for those over 65 years of age costs the same as for category 3. As for levels A, B, and C, these have to do with the proportion of qualified and unskilled workers in the business. Nevertheless, you should know that the employer, in most cases, is the one who pays all the fees for the procedure.

Understanding the costs involved in acquiring a work permit in the UAE

We have already discussed the work permit in UAE cost in terms of applying for and issuing the same. However, some of the documents and requirements for this permit also have a cost. Below you can see some additional costs to obtain a work permit in the country:

  • The offer letter has an average cost of AED 279
  • Emirates ID, AED 370
  • Basic health insurance, AED 700
  • Visa Stamping AED 493

Can mission workers obtain a work permit in the UAE?

The mission work permit in UAE is for foreign workers who will undertake short-term project work. Therefore, according to labor law, these employees are considered to be on probation in the company. Additionally, as an essential requirement, the worker must be outside the country to request the permit and leave after it expires.

However, the employer can apply for a new mission permit after the employee has left the UAE. Moreover, the employer must cancel the work card of the employee before making the new request. Nevertheless, in contrast to the work permits in the UAE, the mission permit can take up to 4 weeks to obtain.

Steps to obtain a mission work permit UAE

Commonly, it is the PRO of the company requesting the service of the worker who makes the request. To apply for a mission work visa in the country, you must follow the steps that we will indicate below:

  1. The company must request the mission visa fee and the application requirements.
  2. After approval of the quota, apply for the mission visa at MOHRE, which is valid for 60 days.
  3. The employee must sign the application.
  4. After the authorities approve the application, you must apply for a mission entry permit.
  5. The employee will then be able to enter the country after receiving the entry permit and will receive UAE visa insurance.
  6. Once in the country, the employee must send a copy of the mission visa to the hiring company.
  7. The employee must then apply for an employment contract and sign it.
  8. Finally, they must submit the contract to MOHRE to obtain approval and a UAE employment card.

What are the requirements you need to present for getting a work permit in the UAE?

The work permit UAE requirements include the documents that we will detail below:

  • Original passport of the worker along with a copy of it.
  • Photograph of the same measurements as those of the passport.
  • Emirates ID.
  • MOHRE entry permit.
  • Medical certificate issued by an authorized health center.
  • Copy of the academic qualifications of the applicant, certified by the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs. They must also certify them at a UAE Embassy in the home country of the employee.
  • Business license and company card of the contracting employer.

Furthermore, the employer is responsible for making the work permit application for the worker. However, the latter is solely responsible for presenting the documentation and requesting the residence permit.

How can I check my work permit approval in UAE?

You can do the work permit UAE check in a few simple steps on the MOHRE website. Next, we will detail the steps you must follow for a quick verification:

  1. Enter on the MOHRE website or application.
  2. Next, you will need to select the work permit status approval service.
  3. Enter your permit number.
  4. Click Search and the system will show you the requested information.

What should I do if my work permit application is rejected in the UAE?

The authorities can deny the worker a permit for different reasons, such as the lack of a document. Therefore, if you get a rejected work permit UAE, you must obtain the information about the rejection. Below you can see a list of common reasons for the denial of a work permit:

  • I did not properly complete the application
  • Does not comply with the requirements of the authorities
  • The worker has some problems with justice
  • Does not have the necessary qualifications
  • You do not have a valid job offer

However, if the reasons have a feasible solution, you can make a new application for the permit. For these cases, it is advisable to seek help from experts in issuing visas or other types of permits in the UAE.

Do I need a no-objection certificate (NOC) for a work permit in UAE?

In short, you do not need an NOC for a work permit in UAE, just the documents mentioned above. In the country, in matters related to work, you only need a No Objection Letter from your employer in the following cases:

  • When you are going to change jobs
  • When you require a change of sponsor
  • If you need to apply for a visa to travel to another country if you have a UAE residence visa

How can I check the status of my work permit application in the UAE?

To check the work permit UAE status, the MOHRE has a website with a very simple interface. Therefore, to carry out the verification you only have to follow the steps that we will detail below:

  1. Go to the MOHRE website (mohre.gov.ae).
  2. Select the menu that indicates the status of the work permit.
  3. Next, you will need to enter the permit or transaction number.
  4. Work permit UAE

Why permit to work is required?

Simply put, the work permit system documents risks that pose harm to safety and health. Specifically, workers, assets, and the environment.

The PTW system complements the internal risk assessment process. Additionally, managers can identify specific tasks that require work permission. On the other hand, workers can request a valid permit and specific instructions regarding the nature of the work.

It is common knowledge that the workflow involves managers issuing documented permissions. All these permits can be on paper or digitalized, to competent workers. Thus, they can perform non-trivial tasks that generally carry greater risk.

After the workers proceed to sign the form, they are authorized to carry out the work. Furthermore, the system is essential for several reasons listed below:

  • Improves safety: Thanks to the issuance of permits to work on dangerous tasks workers are aware of the risks. In addition, being able to have the necessary equipment to carry out the work safely.

The idea is to protect employers from the hefty fines and costs they may incur. Specifically, due to poor training management.

  • Greater responsibility: As this is a documented process, all parties, especially employees and contractors, are aware of the responsibilities and their risks. If an unexpected situation occurs, the document makes it easier for management to identify exactly who is responsible.
  • Improved business processes: The company can use the recorded information to formulate better security procedures. In addition, being able to mitigate security risks by investing in better security equipment and providing training to employees.

Types of permit to work

Depending on the nature of the work, different types of permits are usually used. Currently, there are seven widely used permits in the Permit to Work system:

Hot work permit

A hot permit, you can also find them as hot work permits. They are most commonly used to review, authorize, and approve any type of work that involves fires. Generally, hot permits are for tasks that include an ignition source, such as welding or flame cutting.

On the other hand, there are also cold permits that are broadly for all other work activities that have nothing to do with fires. However, you have to know that they are activities that continue to be a risk for workers.

Common examples of activities that require a cold permit are the use of solvents or chemicals for maintenance or cleaning. In addition, handling resins, corrosive materials, installing scaffolding, or any work that involves heavy physical labor.

Confined space entry permit

A confined space entry permit is required before workers have to perform tasks that require entering or investigating confined spaces. That is ships, conduits, tanks, or even trenches.

The permit must include a description of the processes to prepare the confined space to be entered. In addition, plans for safe worker entry and any restoration work in these particular spaces.

Electrical work permit

Any business that involves contractors or employees coming into contact with live electrical conductors requires an electrical work permit. For instance, maintenance teams working on telecommunications or electrical equipment have to obtain permission before starting their duties.

Within the content of the permits is the area where the work will be carried out, and the personnel involved. In addition, the safety processes and the supervisors who supervise the work.

Excavation permit

Generally, you need an excavation permit for work that involves digging below a certain depth. A common case is 30cm, as digging below the surface can expose workers to specific risks. For example, falling debris, landslides, and gas or electrical lines.

The main reasons why an excavation permit is needed are the following:

  • Safety: Excavation work can be dangerous for employees. Thanks to the permit process you have a guarantee that they are implementing the corresponding security measures. As a result, the risk of accidents in the process is reduced. That is explosions, exposure to harmful substances in the air, and others.
  • Utility Identification: Underground utility lines, such as water, gas, sewer, and power lines, are typically underground.
  • Quality Control: Reporting requirements and inspections are often part of the permit process. Thanks to these steps you have a guarantee that the excavation work is according to the corresponding standard. As a result, the possibility of mediocre work is reduced.

Height work permits in the UAE

Work at height usually requires work at height permits. It is essential to provide safety to employees who will work in elevated positions in general. Especially working at heights greater than 1.8 m or 6 feet where there is a risk of falling. That is to say,

  • Scaffolding: Use, assembly, and disassembly of scaffolding for maintenance or construction work.
  • Tower work: Work on transmission or telecommunications towers, that is, repair, installation, and maintenance.
  • Elevator maintenance and installation: Work on escalators or elevators that often involves work at height when servicing or installing elevator systems.
  • Industrial maintenance: These are special maintenance tasks for machinery, equipment, or industrial structures at height, for example, manufacturing plants.

Chemical handling permit

A work permit for handling chemicals is an essential document in particular industries. For instance, pharmaceutical, chemical manufacturing, petrochemical, and research laboratories. That is, where dangerous chemicals are stored, handled, or processed.

Generally, the chemical handling permit aims to keep employees safe when handling chemicals that may be hazardous.

Radiation work permit

Initially, you need to know that isolation and restoration are essential safety measures if a person is exposed to a radioactive source. For example, radiography, which is a non-destructive testing method that uses ionizing radiation. The idea of ​​this is to inspect the integrity of materials, such as pipes, welds, and other structural components.

All of this, especially to guarantee the safety of personnel and the environment, must have the radiation permit to work. Below, you will see a list of all the reasons why this work system is essential:

  • Radiation safety: The main and most important reason for issuing radiation permits is to ensure the safety of people. Especially those who work with ionizing radiation or those who are exposed to it.

The permit must describe the safety measures and procedures that must be followed to minimize the risk of radiation exposure. Especially because of all the harmful effects on health.

  • Radiation Dose Limits: The idea of ​​these permits is to establish and enforce dose limits for the public and workers. Thanks to these limits, people can be protected from excessive exposure to radiation, which can have health effects.
  • Equipment Safety: Radiation permits typically require regular maintenance and calibration of radiation-emitting equipment. Specifically, to ensure its proper functioning and production of accurate results without excessive radiation exposure.

Permit to work systems

Overview of PTW systems

It is important that you know a permit to work definition to better understand how these systems work. Therefore, this is special authorization documentation that ensures that the appropriate risk has been accessed for the process.

Additionally, a level of control is established to reduce the severity, probability, and potential for an incident to occur. This can be regulatory requirements, general best practices, or company policies.

Therefore, a permit to work (PTW) system is a process for keeping employees safe in hazardous operations. In this way, risks must be evaluated, and an adequate security protocol and adequate communication must be established throughout the process.

A PTW system is designed to mitigate health, environmental, sustainability, and safety risks in certain operations. Therefore, they must adapt to changes that may arise.

This way, employees can earn money in the UAE for their families and not suffer any accidents in the process.

Digital vs paper-based systems

  • Systems that are paper-based are very prone to errors due to manual entry of all data. However, with a digital system, this data is entered and validated automatically, reducing the risk of any errors.
  • It provides better visibility into the entire permitting process, making it easier to identify security hazards and mitigate risks. Additionally, the digital system may include alarms and security controls that are automated and mandatory.
  • The digital system creates an audit trail of all activities. This way, it can be tracked and audited at any time without data extraction; including who created, reviewed, approved, and closed the corresponding permission.
  • Digital systems allow for real-time communication between all people involved in the permit process. This can improve collaboration and reduce any delays.
  • A digitalized system helps streamline and automate the permit process, reducing the time and effort necessary to issue permits. Therefore, this offers a cost reduction for the company.

Integration with safety management systems

A PTW system is not independent. In addition, it can be integrated with much broader security management systems in companies. Therefore, this integration allows for consistency in security practices, aligning the PTW process with other security protocols.

Thanks to the synergy of these systems, a better comprehensive security culture is promoted, emphasizing proactive risk management and continuous improvement.

Security professionals must understand the nuances of the PTW system and its integration with security protocols. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the PTW system will depend on careful planning and risk assessment.

In this way, companies not only meet regulatory requirements but also foster a safety-first culture.

Real-time monitoring and reporting

A digital system offers you great visibility in real-time of the status and progress of activities related to these permits. This way, through simple dashboards, notifications, and the ability to generate reports, they can track these permissions from start to finish.

Additionally, you can very accurately track the workers involved in the permitted work. This way, you can ensure that tasks are assigned to trained and authorized people.

Thanks to this, a culture of responsibility and safety awareness is fostered.

Benefits of implementing permit to work systems

PTW systems provide you with a structured and documented approach. This way, you can manage workplace activities that can be very dangerous. Additionally, it serves as a fundamental part of achieving a safe workplace.

Thus, like the new visa rules, these systems offer a wide range of benefits. For this reason, so that you understand more about the good things about PTW systems, we will explain the best benefits.

Enhanced safety culture

A PTW system is a process that helps keep all employees safe during all risky and non-standard operations. Therefore, you must evaluate the risks, establish proper communication during the process, and establish a good security protocol.

For this reason, a PTW system is designed so that all health, environmental, safety, and sustainability risks are mitigated in specific operations. In this way, a better safety culture is created in the work environment.

Prevention of accidents and incidents

Thanks to PTW systems, companies can ensure that employers, employees, and contractors are always protected when performing high-risk tasks. All this over a period of time and with specific precautions.

Additionally, it allows the process of taking necessary precautions to be done before performing tasks. These tasks include hot and cold work, work in confined spaces, electrical work, etc.

Among the features are:

  • Ensure that working conditions are the safest for employees. This way, security leaders can control and coordinate the work.
  • Facilitate collaboration between multiple teams and enable the generation of composite PTWs where multiple high-risk tasks may need to be completed at the same time.
  • Maintain and manage all forms to generate the PTW. Additionally, it allows safety leaders to verify the skill levels of any worker and ensure any work can be completed on time.

Legal compliance and regulatory alignment

When you create a centralized platform to manage permissions and security-related data, you gain many benefits. Therefore, it can ensure better decision-making and better compliance.

Thanks to this, the chances of accidents or any legal problems are reduced. Additionally, they can reduce the risks posed by manual data entry; greatly improving the accuracy of the information within the permits.

Therefore, you can avoid any financial sanctions or fines towards your company if you fail to comply with this system. Plus, it saves you from having to do extra paperwork by manually filling out all this information.

Improved communication and coordination

Thanks to these systems, real-time communication is allowed between all the parties that are involved in this process. Additionally, this allows for huge improvements and reduced delays.

Therefore, a permit process that is driven by this system helps avoid miscommunication and any misunderstandings. In this way, much smoother and faster processing times are obtained.

In addition, this guarantees that everyone has access to information in real time. This is why these PTW systems improve the work environment in companies.

Enhanced efficiency and productivity

PTW systems greatly reduce the time spent completing and processing paperwork. Approvals can therefore be granted in a shorter time and work can begin sooner.

Additionally, thanks to the improvement in communication between teams, everyone has instant access to information. In this way, a work environment is created that is more effective and productive.

On the other hand, having permits on time and the entire process following established safety standards allows employees to perform much better. In this way, by having security control over security processes, you can work more productively in less time.

FAQs

Is a work permit mandatory in the UAE?

Yes. A valid work permit is required to work legally in the UAE in 2026. Working without it leads to fines, job bans, or deportation.

Who issues work permits in the UAE?

The Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation issues work permits. The employer applies for it on behalf of the employee.

Can I work in UAE without a work permit?

No. Working without a work permit is illegal, even with a job offer or a visit visa. Employment must start only after approval.

How long does it take to get a UAE work permit?

Processing usually takes 5 to 10 working days in 2026 if documents are complete. Delays happen when approvals or attestations are missing.

Is work permit different from employment visa?

Yes. A work permit allows employment approval, while an employment visa allows legal stay in the UAE. Both are required to work legally.

What happens if a work permit expires?

Work must stop immediately after expiry. Late renewal leads to fines, legal issues, and possible visa cancellation.

title: Temporary Work Permits UAE: The Ultimate Employment Guide
content:
Table of Contents

Toggle
  • Eligibility Criteria for Temporary Work Permits
  • Application Process for Temporary Work Permits
  • Understanding Temporary Work Permit Fees or Cost
  • Temporary work Permit UAE Benefits
  • Temporary Work Permit UAE Requirements
    • Documents Required for Temporary work permit UAE
  • Rights and Restrictions of Temporary Workers
  • Renewal and Extension Procedures
    • Temporary work permit UAE Extension
  • Impact on Employment Market and Economy
  • Temporary work Permit UAE Cancellation
  • Common FAQs about Temporary Work Permits
    • What is a temporary work permit in the UAE?
    • Who is eligible to apply for a temporary work permit?
    • How long is a UAE temporary work permit valid?
    • What documents are required for a temporary work permit?
    • How much does a temporary work permit cost in the UAE?
    • Can a temporary work permit be converted into a residence visa?

Through a temporary work permit UAE, a foreigner with a residence visa can work on a short-term project. However, you must meet the requirements of the Ministry of Labor (currently MOHRE) to obtain the permit. Nevertheless, it is not the potential employee who carries out the procedures and pays the fees, but the potential employer.

In this article, we will show you in detail the process of obtaining a work permit in the country. In the same way, you will learn all the information about the fees and other requirements to obtain this permit.

Eligibility Criteria for Temporary Work Permits

Receiving a temporary work permit UAE depends on the applicant meeting the eligibility criteria. In this case, if you do not meet the criteria, you will waste your time and money as they will not authorize the permit. The authorities have established two basic and invariable requirements to be able to obtain one of these permits:

  • Applicant for the temporary work permit must be at least 18 years of age.
  • You must be a resident of the country (citizen or possess a residence visa).

Other criteria and terms apply for those who wish to obtain this service, such as the age limit of 65 years. However, we detail the other characteristics of this service later to see if you are eligible.

Application Process for Temporary Work Permits

Due to the nature of this permit, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratization (MOHRE) is the one who grants it. Nonetheless, companies should know that this permit is only for work for a certain time, that is, it is short-term. Additionally, the entire application process and payment of fees is the responsibility of the employer of the applicant.

The employer can apply on the MOHRE website or app, or at TAW-SEEL centres. The process of applying for a temporary work permit UAE consists of the following and simple steps:

  1. When applying online, you can use your username and password or the UAE Pass.
  2. Then, the MOHRE receives the request from the company that wants the services of a professional worker.
  3. If you did not send a document or have problems with one, you will receive a notification to resolve the situation.
  4. Then, if everything is in order, the MOHRE will approve the issuance of the permit.
  5. Immediately afterward, the Ministry will approve the employment contract.
  6. Pay the applicable fees.

The temporary work permit processing time is approximately 2 days, then you will receive confirmation of approval. However, you can track your request through the same MOHRE website or application. In the same way, you can request information about the permit and your application from the call center at 600590000.

Understanding Temporary Work Permit Fees or Cost

The temporary work permit UAE cost includes an issuance fee by the authorities of AED 300. Additionally, the cost includes a 5% value-added tax, as well as additional charges if the sponsor is within the country. These include knowledge and innovation costs of AED 10 each.

On the other hand, requests made through MOHRE digital media have no cost. However, there are federal fees of AED 50, and if you apply at a service center, AED 72. Furthermore, these prices and fees may change without notice, so please check before starting the process.

Temporary work Permit UAE Benefits

The temporary work permit UAE benefits are several for workers who manage to obtain approval. Some of the advantages of obtaining one of these permits are listed below:

  • You will be able to work for a company in the UAE for at least 6 months.
  • You will gain quantifiable experience in the professional field in which you work.
  • Working for 6 months (or a year if you extend the permit) will help you get used to the culture and environment of the UAE.
  • You will be able to develop your skills in a favorable work environment.
  • The experience will help you attract the attention of employers both in the UAE and in your home country.
  • It could help you obtain long-term employment in important locations such as Abu Dhabi, Dubai, or Sharjah.

Temporary Work Permit UAE Requirements

To obtain this permit, you must meet the temporary work permit UAE requirements. Next, we will show you the terms and conditions, as well as the documents necessary for the application:

  • As we mentioned above, the applicant must be over 18 years of age.
  • Labor legislation requires compliance with the requirements for certain professions and those that require a professional license.
  • The authorized signatory of the company must handle the application process.
  • The employee can only obtain a permit if the activity for which they are hired has directly to do with their profession.
  • Having a current business license is essential for the contracting business.
  • The contracting company must have no violations of the regulations or laws of the Emirates to avoid any suspension.
  • The company can apply for the temporary work permit UAE once and can apply for it again once it expires.
  • The current employer must approve the electronic form (this excludes employees with pending court cases).
  • The permit applies to all skill levels and professions.

Documents Required for Temporary work permit UAE

Applying for a temporary work permit UAE also requires the submission of various documents by the applicant. Thus, you must have on hand, before the employer begins the process, the following documents:

  • Photograph of the worker on a white background.
  • Copy of the passport, which must have an expiration period equal to or greater than 6 months from the date of application.
  • Employment contract form signed by both parties.
  • Academic certificates for applicants who fall within levels 1 and 2 (Bachelor’s degree or higher). The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation must endorse the said certificate.
  • A professional license issued by the corresponding authority. This includes the Ministry of Health, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Justice, and other authorities in the country.
  • Labor court form for employees with cases pending in said court.
  • No Objection Letter (known as NOC) for a work permit.

Rights and Restrictions of Temporary Workers

The temporary work permit UAE allows workers to enjoy certain advantages but with restrictions as well. Below, you can see what this type of permit does and does not allow for foreigners who obtain it:

  • The permit helps you work in the UAE but only for the stipulated time, which is 6 months.
  • You may only work for the sponsoring company while the permit lasts.
  • This permit is also used to work part-time in a company other than the main one you currently work for. However, you need approval from your current employer as it is part of the application process for such cases.
  • If you have not received and signed an employment contract with an employer, you will not obtain the permit. Likewise, it is strictly necessary that you be a resident of the UAE, so you must have a residence visa.
  • You can only carry out work related to your profession; otherwise the authorities can do the temporary work permit UAE cancellation.

Renewal and Extension Procedures

Renewing a Temporary work permit UAE is the same as applying for the first time by the employer. Therefore, it can only be done once the previous permission is completed through the following steps:

  1. To begin, the employee must provide the employer with the permit renewal application form.
  2. Then, you must provide all the documents, which you should have in person as they are basically the initial application documents.
  3. The employer must continue the process by paying the necessary fees.
  4. Finally, the company must submit the renewal application to the MOHRE or the entity in charge in the corresponding Free Zone.

Temporary work permit UAE Extension

The extension process also involves the same steps as the initial application and the same documentation. Additionally, you must submit a No Objection Letter from your current employer to work at another company. Once all this is obtained, the new employer must complete the entire permit application process.

Impact on Employment Market and Economy

The UAE authorities have created different ways to ensure opportunities for its skilled workforce. However, Emirati professionals have certain limitations in both the public and private sectors. Furthermore, difficulties in moving from the public to the private sector are a common problem.

The temporary work permit UAE is a solution for both nationals and foreigners in the country. Nevertheless, many companies prefer to hire foreign personnel because they are more likely to find qualified workers. Furthermore, as is the case with a standard work permit, the company must prove that an Emirati cannot occupy such a position.

This type of competition has often caused us to not value the skills and professionalism of Emirati citizens. However, the authorities continue to improve opportunities for national professionals, such as the Emiratization program. This scheme induces companies to meet an annual quota of 2% of Emirati workers in their businesses.

Temporary work Permit UAE Cancellation

After the regulatory time for the stay of the worker has ended, the employer must cancel the temporary work permit. Next, you can see what the process of temporary work permit UAE cancellation is like in a few simple steps:

  1. The employer must submit the cancellation request, through a form signed by the employee, to the MOHRE.
  2. Next, you must upload the necessary documents.
  3. The Ministry processes the application and sends it to the GDRFA (General Directorate of Residency and Foreign Affairs).
  4. Finally, the GDRFA cancels the residence visa, informing the MOHRE to cancel the permit.

Common FAQs about Temporary Work Permits

What is a temporary work permit in the UAE?

It is a short-term permit that allows individuals to work legally in the UAE for a specific employer and duration.

Who is eligible to apply for a temporary work permit?

Employees hired for short-term projects, probation roles, or specific assignments are eligible to apply for temporary work permits.

How long is a UAE temporary work permit valid?

It is usually valid for up to six months, depending on the approved employment terms.

What documents are required for a temporary work permit?

A passport copy, photograph, employment contract, and employer-related documents are required documents for a temporary work permit.

How much does a temporary work permit cost in the UAE?

The cost varies based on employee category and government fees.

Can a temporary work permit be converted into a residence visa?

Yes, it can be converted if the employer meets eligibility requirements and applies for a residence visa.

title: 7 Things to Know About Part-Time Work Permits in the UAE
content:
Table of Contents

Toggle
  • 1) Eligibility Criteria
  • 2) Cost of Part-Time Work Permit
  • 3) Application Process of Part-Time Work Permit
  • 4) Requirements for Part-Time Work Permit
  • 5) Benefits of Part-Time Work Permit
  • 6) Part-Time Work Permit in UAE Renewal and Extension
  • 7) Part-Time Work Permit in UAE Cancellation Process
  • How Connect Zone Can Help?
  • FAQs
    • What is a part-time work permit in the UAE?
    • Who is eligible for a UAE part-time work permit?
    • Can students apply for a part-time work permit in the UAE?
    • How long is a part-time work permit valid?
    • What documents are required for a part-time work permit?
    • Can a full-time employee work part-time legally in the UAE?

Starting in 2010, employers can apply for a part-time work permit in UAE at MOHRE. In this way, they can hire staff for up to one year to perform specific tasks during that time. A part-time work permit allows workers to work in two companies simultaneously.

This article will explain all about this part-time work permit and how to obtain one. You will also find the cost of a part-time work permit in the UAE, application procedures, and requirements in detail.

1) Eligibility Criteria

To work part-time, a foreigner must obtain a part-time work permit in the UAE. It’s a mandatory requirement for legal employment in the UAE. Employees can acquire this permit and work in two companies full-time and part-time with some specific conditions with a one-year validity. However, the employees are not allowed to work in two companies at the same time without this permit in the UAE. In case of failure, the employer must pay the hefty penalties and may face legal complexities according to the UAE labor laws.

Additionally, workers must comply with the following part-time work permit UAE requirements:

  • Minimum age. People who request the permit must be over 18 years old, or they will not be able to receive it.
  • Residence visa. The applicant must have a valid UAE residence visa to apply for the permit.
  • If the expatriate worker is in the country on a family visa, they can also apply for one of these permits.
  • Persons holding a tourist visa in the UAE are not eligible.
  • People over 65 cannot apply for a temporary work permit in the country.

2) Cost of Part-Time Work Permit

The part-time work permits in UAE cost AED 600 according to the two rates that make it up. Next, we will show you what the two rates consist of that you must pay to issue the service:

  • The permit application fee is AED 100.
  • The approval fee is AED 500.

However, it is not the employee who must pay the fees above. The employer must take charge. Moreover, permit fees are separate from those related to the Tahseel service. This service includes an AED 72 business center fee and an AED 50 federal fee.

3) Application Process of Part-Time Work Permit

The employer is responsible for applying for the Part time work permit UAE for the future employee. To carry out this procedure, you can choose two methods. The first is to visit a Tahseel center. On the other hand, we explain the second method, which is through the MOHRE website:

  1. Log in to the official website of regulated authorities with your credentials.
  2. Request through the available service delivery channels.
  3. Then, the Ministry will verify the compliance of the applicant with the requirements and documents.
  4. The requesting establishment will receive notification about the deficits.
  5. Next, if everything is in order, the corresponding authority will issue the part-time work permit.
  6. They will then approve the contract in electronic format.
  7. Lastly, you will need to pay federal permit processing fees.

4) Requirements for Part-Time Work Permit

The part-time work permits UAE requirements include the following documents:

  • Color photograph with a white background.
  • A valid employee’s passport copy.
  • A valid job offer letter signed by both parties.
  • Copies of the business licenses of the contracting companies (the primary or current one and the secondary or applicant).
  • A bachelor’s degree certificate or higher is required for first and second-level skills.
  • You will need a graduate diploma or higher certification for third or fourth-level skills.
  • Likewise, for skill level 5, you will need a high school certificate.
  • For skill levels 6 through 9, no certificate is required.
  • Specialized professionals, such as physicians, mentors, lawyers, and engineers, must obtain professional licenses from relevant authorities.
  • A valid employment contract copy.
  • The NOC from the recent employer.
  • A valid visa from the sponsor.

All the above documents are required for the permit and must be approved by the regulated authorities to apply for this part-time work permit.

5) Benefits of Part-Time Work Permit

Apart from your full-time job, you can get a part-time work permit UAE benefits. Thus, if you obtain permission from MOHRE, you can enjoy the following advantages:

  • You can work part-time in any of the job options offered by companies.
  • This permit allows you to earn extra income apart from your regular full-time job.
  • You can learn new skills and earn more experience in your special field with a part-time work opportunity.
  • You can add relevant experience to your resume with this part-time work.

6) Part-Time Work Permit in UAE Renewal and Extension

You can only renew a Part-time work permit in UAE after the previous permit expires. Furthermore, you can only renew the permit once for the same duration, that is, for another six months until completing one year. In the case of an extension, the employee must have the consent of the current employer to complete the process.

To renew the temporary work permit, you must follow the procedure that we will indicate below:

  1. The employee must submit the permit renewal application form.
  2. Attach the same documents required for applying for the first time.
  3. Pay service fees.
  4. The employer must apply for the MOHRE in person or through their official website.

On the other hand, to extend the permit and be able to continue working part-time in another company, follow the steps that we will indicate:

  1. The employer must consent to the employee requesting an extension of the part-time work permit.
  2. Next, the new employer must request permission for the worker.
  3. The MOHRE will verify if the worker meets the eligibility requirements and will issue a new permit for six months.

In both cases, you must remember that you can only make requests once, after which you will have no further chances.

7) Part-Time Work Permit in UAE Cancellation Process

If you want to do the part-time work permit UAE cancellation, the process is very simple. In addition, you only have to meet a few requirements, which are the following:

  • A letter from the concerned authority (in this case, the MOHRE) declaring the cancellation of the permit.
  • A copy of the original work permit.

However, you can only complete this process in person at one of the AMER Centers during established business hours. Likewise, the service cost is AED 50 + VAT, and it takes about 48 hours to receive the response. Next, you will see the permission cancellation process, which includes a few steps:

  1. Go to one of the nearest AMER Centers.
  2. Then, at the center reception, you must choose the type of service you require and, in this case, request the cancellation of the permit.
  3. Submit the documents we mentioned above.
  4. Next, pay the service fees.
  5. Finally, apply.

After completing the process, you will have to wait about 48 hours to receive the response about the Part-time work permit in UAE. Once the authorities cancel the permit, the worker cannot continue working unless he makes a new request if he has not exhausted the permits.

How Connect Zone Can Help?

Due to the change made in the UAE labor law, foreign workers residing in the country can work part-time jobs. However, they must apply for a part-time work permit in UAE, which the company they will be working for must do. Additionally, it is necessary to have a residence visa and the NOC of the current employer in the country.

We can help you learn about this documentation and other processes related to the business world. At Connect Zone, we can help you. In this way, our group of experts offers you valuable information just by contacting us.

FAQs

What is a part-time work permit in the UAE?

It allows legal part-time employment alongside a main job or studies.

Who is eligible for a UAE part-time work permit?

Students, residents, and full-time employees meeting criteria qualify.

Can students apply for a part-time work permit in the UAE?

Yes, students aged 18 and above can apply.

How long is a part-time work permit valid?

Usually valid for one year.

What documents are required for a part-time work permit?

Passport, visa, Emirates ID, and employer approval.

Can a full-time employee work part-time legally in the UAE?

Yes, with employer consent and MOHRE approval.

acceptedAnswer.text: A part-time work permit is an official authorization from MOHRE that allows a resident to work fewer hours or days than a full-time employee. It also enables working for more than one employer legally.

mainEntity.name: Who is eligible for a UAE part-time work permit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Eligibility includes students (15+), residents on family sponsorship, and full-time employees with a valid residency visa. In 2026, even skilled professionals on visit visas can transition to this permit after status change.

mainEntity.name: Can students apply for a part-time work permit in the UAE?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, students aged 15 and above can apply. Students between 15-18 require guardian consent and a medical fitness certificate, while those 18+ can apply directly through their university or employer NOC.

mainEntity.name: How long is a part-time work permit valid?

acceptedAnswer.text: The permit is typically valid for one year and is renewable. For specific training or student projects, a shorter 3-month permit is also available.

mainEntity.name: What documents are required for a part-time work permit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Required documents include a colored photo, passport copy (6 months validity), Emirates ID, NOC from the primary sponsor, and the signed job offer form from the new employer.

mainEntity.name: Can a full-time employee work part-time legally in the UAE?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, full-time employees can take a second job part-time if they obtain an NOC from their current employer and a part-time permit from MOHRE.

    • Do foreigners need a local sponsor in Dubai?

Starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner is possible given that the UAE has launched several initiatives that promote foreign investment. However, if you want to have a smooth entry into the UAE market, you should follow the right steps.

In this article, you will learn more about how to start a business in Dubai as a foreigner. Furthermore, if you are wondering why should you start business in Dubai as a foreigner, you will see all the reasons.

Can You Have Full Ownership of Your Company in Dubai?

First of all, you may be wondering: Can Foreigners Start A Business In Dubai? The truth is that across the UAE you will find many different types of businesses run by foreigners. So, as a foreign investor, you can start your business easily.

However, when it comes to starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner there is another crucial question. You may be wondering if you may have full ownership of your company.

This matter is highly important for investors, as they do not want to split the shares with another one. In this regard, the law regarding full ownership has changed over the years.

Previously, it was only allowed for some activities in the professional sector and for companies established in the Free Zone. However, with the latest amendments, foreign investors can now have 100% ownership of their businesses according to the following:

  • Natural and legal persons can now establish a company and get total ownership in Dubai mainland.
  • It is required to have a Local Service Agent (LSA) which is different from a sponsor, as an LSA does not have shares in your company.
  • It is only allowed for 1,061 economic activities, so you have to check if you qualify.

Which is the most profitable business in UAE?

If you are starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner, you may be considering the most successful business opportunities, as this allows you to increase the likelihood of success.

The good news is that, since Dubai is a thriving city with a solid economy, almost any type of business is bound to succeed. You just have to make good entrepreneurial decisions so you can increase your popularity and profit.

However, there are some sectors that are on the rise, and it is worth considering them if you plan to operate in Dubai:

  • Ecommerce
  • Education & Training
  • Retail and Fashion
  • IT Services
  • Real Estate
  • Tourism
  • Food and beverage
  • Art
  • Health and wellness

Why Consider Dubai for Your Business Venture?

In the UAE there are 7 Emirates, and more than 40 free zones. As you can see, there are many options for you to start your business.

However, why should you start business in Dubai as a foreigner? This enchanting location has a promising market and it is considered a commercial hub in the Middle East. Therefore, if you want to take advantage of your business location, then Dubai is your go-to option.

The following are the best reasons why you should set Dubai as the location for your business:

  • Strategic location in the Middle East
  • Easy connectivity to Africa, Asia and the Gulf
  • Top infrastructure
  • Friendly policies for businesses
  • Safe living environment
  • Access to technology and innovation
  • Lucrative city

Exploring Free Zones: What Are the Perks of Setting Up Shop There?

In Dubai, there are around 26 Free Zones where investors can establish their businesses. So, if you want to set up your business in a free zone, instead of in Dubai Mainland, you can access additional benefits.

Some of the perks of free zones are the following:

  • No import and export taxes
  • No currency regulations
  • High level of confidentiality
  • Total ownership of your business, regardless of the economic activity
  • No limitations on trade
  • Several office and warehouse options
  • Easy incorporation process
  • Excellent infrastructure

Let’s Talk Business Structure: How to Set Up Your Company

When starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner, you have to decide the structure of your business. This means that you have to take into account the following:

  • Business activity: what activity do you want to carry out? Is it on the list of permitted activities? Do you need to add more than one or two business activities to your license?
  • Purpose of your company: set clear goals and prepare a business plan on what you want to achieve.
  • Operational aspect: do you plan to operate locally or online? Have you considered what type of office do you need?
  • Corporate structure: consider the type of legal entity you want to incorporate by doing extensive research.

Checking Out Your Options: What Are the Legal Structures for Foreign Businesses in Dubai?

The first step in how to start a business in Dubai as a foreigner is to decide which type of company you would like to incorporate.

Every type of entity has its advantages, so you have to decide which one better suits the nature of your business. In addition, some of these business structures are only reserved for UAE Nationals or GCC nationals, so keep in mind that as a foreigner you may have some restrictions in this matter.

The business structure available is the following:

  • Sole proprietorship: foreigners need an LSA to open this type of company when it is aimed at the commercial or industrial sector. If it is in the professional sector, it is not necessary.
  • Limited Liability Company (LLC): This is the most used form of company. It can be formed with at least 2 shareholders and a maximum of 50.
  • Branch of a foreign company: it is not a separate entity from the parent company, but a dedicated outlet in the UAE.

Where to Base Your Business: Navigating Jurisdiction in Dubai

Once you have considered the nature of your business and the type of legal entity, the next step will be to decide on the jurisdiction.

When starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner you have two main options: Mainland or Free Zone. You could opt for Dubai Mainland or any of the Dubai Free Zones. Since this may be a tough choice, you have to consider the following:

  • Market access: mainland jurisdiction offers a broader audience as you are allowed to operate within the UAE. Whereas with a free zone company, you can only trade internationally.
  • Target market: if your customers are mainly local, then you should opt for a mainland setup. But, if your clients are predominantly global, then you have to opt for a free zone.
  • Legal requirements: consider which legal framework is more suitable for your business as there are different regulations across free zones.
  • Ownership: if you want full ownership, consider if your economic activity is allowed for 100% control in the mainland. If not, then you better opt for a free zone.
  • Costs: free zone costs tend to be fixed whereas mainland are variable.

Finding the Right License: Understanding Your Options

After you have considered the jurisdiction where you want to incorporate your company, then you need to evaluate the type of license you will need.

When starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner you have the following licenses available:

  • Commercial license: for trading businesses and commercial-related activities
  • Professional license: for businesses offering service-oriented services.
  • Industrial license: for companies working in the manufacturing and industrial sectors.
  • Tourism license: for businesses in the tourism and hospitality sector.

Ready to Dive In? Here Are the Steps to Kickstart Your Business in Dubai as a Non-Resident

Having an overall view of all of the requirements for starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner will help you navigate the incorporation process easily.

By knowing all the steps, you have to go through, you can prepare your documentation and decide the best route for your business.

Step 1: Figure Out What Type of Business You Want

First of all, you have to think about what type of business you want to launch in the UAE. Consider the following:

  • Business activity
  • Jurisdiction
  • Legal structure
  • License type

In case you want to incorporate an LLC in Dubai, you may have to submit different documentation than for other type of legal structure.

Step 2: Pick a Catchy Name for Your Venture

Once you have decided on the type of business, you have to choose a trading name. Keep in mind you have to follow the regulations established, which are the following:

  • The name cannot be already registered or in use by another company
  • It must comply with your business activities
  • You have to include the acronym of the business structure you have selected at the end of the name
  • It should not violate the public order or values of the country

Step 3: Get Your License Sorted

If you are in a Free Zone, apply for the business license directly to the respective authority, and if you are in Dubai, apply at the DED.

Keep in mind there are the cheapest trade licenses in the UAE, so you do not have to exceed your budget to start operating.

Step 4: Register Your Business and Get It Officially Incorporated

Next, you have to prepare your application form for registering your company. Make sure to gather the documentation required to submit it too. Ensure you have the following:

  • Business documentation
  • Identity proofs
  • Trade license
  • Permissions

Step 5: Secure Your Business Visa to Get Going

As a foreign investor, you need to have a residence visa to be able to work and live in the UAE. You can apply for a long-term visa and also for your dependents and members of your company.

Lastly, you also have to consider opening a business bank account in Dubai so you can manage your finances efficiently.

Breaking Down the Costs: What to Expect When Starting a Business in Dubai as an Expat

When it comes to starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner, you have to consider the costs so you can prepare your budget in advance.

The starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner cost varies depending on several factors, such as the following:

  • Type of legal structure
  • License and activities
  • Location and jurisdiction
  • Business size

In this regard, incorporating a company can be as cheap as AED 10,000 and the price can go up to AED 35,000.

There are low-cost business setup options in Dubai, so you can save money while incorporating your desired company.

Navigating Approvals: What You Need to Launch Your Business as a Foreigner in Dubai

Can Foreigners Start a Business in Dubai? Yes, they can, as Dubai welcomes investors. However, keep in mind that to run your company you may need additional approvals.

Some businesses need governmental permits to operate in Dubai, and these may be the following:

  • Dubai Municipality: approval for food businesses.
  • Dubai Tourism and Commerce Marketing: this is for cafes or hotels.
  • DED (Department of Dubai Economic Development): NOC for required businesses.
  • Dubai Police General Headquarters: for businesses selling liquor.
  • Telecommunication Regulatory Authority: type approval.

If you are not sure about how to get approvals, business setup consultants can assist you in your company’s formation. This way, you can relax while they take care of the most complex legal paperwork.

Don’t Go It Alone: Why Seeking Expert Assistance Is Key

Starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner requires having extensive knowledge about the procedures to follow.

For this reason, seeking assistance from experts can be a great option to improve your success. In addition, experts can help you minimize risk when navigating UAE Labour regulations.

Some of the areas where experts can assist you are the following:

  • Deciding the best legal structure based on your business
  • Choosing the type of activities, you can carry out in the UAE
  • Deciding the proper jurisdiction based on your target market
  • Assisting in incorporating and registering your company

Also, they can help you with starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner cost, as they can provide cost-effective solutions.

What’s the Deal with Local Sponsors? Do You Really Need One?

In some cases, depending on the nature of your business, you may need to appoint a local sponsor. In other cases, you may need support from a Local Service Agent.

You need a sponsor in the following sectors:

  • Oil production and exploration
  • Banking in finances
  • Water and electricity
  • Fishing
  • Printing and Publishing
  • Commercial agency
  • Medical retail and pharmacies
  • Road and air transport

On the other hand, you need a LSA in the following scenarios:

  • When you are incorporating a company in the mainland and need a commercial or industrial license
  • In some economic activities where 100% ownership is allowed but only with an LSA.

Getting a Helping Hand: What Support Is Available for Foreign Entrepreneurs in Dubai?

The Ministry of Economy in the UAE supports foreign businesses by implementing different initiatives. Some of them are the following:

  • Government programs by entities supporting start-ups, and SMEs
  • Residency programs
  • Instant licenses
  • Tech support
  • Support for female entrepreneurs
  • Consultation and mentorship
  • Project launch assistance
  • Loan assistance

Gathering Your Paperwork: Essential Documents for Starting Your Business in Dubai as a Foreigner

The documentation you need to start your business is the following:

  • Passport copies for each shareholder.
  • Passport-sized photograph
  • UAE Residence Visa (if applicable)
  • Emirates ID (if applicable)
  • MOA and Certificate of Incorporation

Bringing in Talent: Are There Rules About Hiring Foreign Employees?

To hire foreign employees in your company, you need to comply with the following:

  • Registered business: your company has to be legally registered in the UAE.
  • Business license: you must have a valid business license.
  • Quote: You should apply for a quota for foreign employees, as in the UAE you also must hire UAE nationals.
  • Contract: both parties should sign the contract and it must be in Arabic and English.
  • Work permit: you should apply for a work permit for employees overseas.
  • Visa: you have to sponsor the residence visa for your employee.

Starting a business in Dubai as a foreigner can be daunting. There are many regulations to follow and if you are not familiar with them, you may face non-compliance issues. For this reason, it is useful to have experts backing your decisions.

Contact us now to help you set up your business smoothly, so you can expand confidently to the UAE as a foreign investor.

FAQs

Can foreigners start a business in Dubai?

Definitely. Foreigners can fully own businesses in Dubai in most sectors.

What are the requirements for foreigners to start a business in Dubai?

These are the documents required to start a business in Dubai: passport copies, a business plan, and approvals are required.

Do foreigners need a local sponsor in Dubai?

Not necessarily. Most activities no longer require sponsors.

Which business structure is best for foreigners in Dubai?

LLCs and free zone companies are popular choices for foreigners.

How long does business setup take for foreigners in Dubai?

Foreigners can set up their businesses in Dubai within one to three weeks.

mainEntity.name: Can foreigners start a business in Dubai?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, foreigners can start and 100% own businesses in Dubai. Whether it is a Free Zone company or a Mainland LLC, recent reforms have removed the mandatory requirement for a local Emirati partner in over 1,000 commercial and industrial activities.

mainEntity.name: What are the requirements for foreigners to start a business in Dubai?

acceptedAnswer.text: The main requirements include: 1. Passport copy of the owner. 2. A clear business activity selection. 3. Three trade name options. 4. Proof of address (Ejari for Mainland or Flexi-desk for Free Zones). 5. Initial approval from the Department of Economy and Tourism (DET).

mainEntity.name: Do foreigners need a local sponsor in Dubai?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, for the majority of sectors, a local sponsor is no longer required. For some professional activities, you might still need a 'Local Service Agent' (LSA), but they have 0% ownership and only handle government paperwork for a fixed annual fee.

mainEntity.name: Which business structure is best for foreigners in Dubai?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you want to trade directly within the UAE market and bid for government projects, a Mainland LLC is best. If your business is focused on international trade or tech services with lower setup costs, a Free Zone company is the preferred choice.

mainEntity.name: How long does business setup take for foreigners in Dubai?

acceptedAnswer.text: With the 2026 digital systems, Free Zone setup can be completed in 3 to 7 working days. Mainland company registration typically takes 10 to 15 working days, depending on office space verification and external approvals.
